Smoothed SHmax on a grid after Hansen & Mount (1990) / Müller et al. (2003)

Source: R/interpolation.R
smooth.Rd

Spatial smoothing of SHmax orientations with a distance-weighted, robust smoother. lambda balances smoothness against fit to the data. Two kernels are available: "fsr" (fixed search radius) and "fnn" (fixed number of nearest neighbours).

Usage

circular_smooth(
  x,
  grid = NULL,
  lon_range = NULL,
  lat_range = NULL,
  gridsize = 2,
  method = c("fsr", "fnn"),
  R_range = 300,
  lambda = 0.5,
  n_iter = 20,
  tol = 1e-06,
  robust_scale_deg = 10,
  min_data = 3L,
  min_sq = 0,
  min_dist_threshold = Inf,
  quality_weighting = FALSE,
  qp = 1
)

PoR_circular_smooth(
  x,
  PoR,
  grid = NULL,
  PoR_grid = TRUE,
  lon_range = NULL,
  lat_range = NULL,
  gridsize = 2.5,
  remove_PoR = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

sf object containing

azi

angles in degrees (e.g. orientation of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\))

unc

(optional) Uncertainties of azi in degree

type

(optional) Methods used for the determination of the direction of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\)

grid

(optional) Point object of class sf.

lon_range, lat_range

(optional) numeric vector specifying the minimum and maximum longitudes and latitudes (ignored if grid is specified).

gridsize

numeric. Target spacing of the regular grid in decimal degree. Default is 2.5. (is ignored if grid is specified)

method

Kernel type: "fsr" (fixed search radius) or "fnn" (fixed number of nearest neighbours).

R_range

numeric. For method = "fsr": search radii in km. For method = "fnn": number of nearest neighbours. Can also be a vector of different radii.

lambda

numeric. Smoothness parameter. lambda > 1 favours smoothness; lambda < 1 favours fidelity to the data.

n_iter

integer. Maximum number of fitting iterations.

tol

numeric. Convergence tolerance on the doubled angle (radians).

robust_scale_deg

numeric. Minimum robustness scale in degrees. The robust cutoff is 6 times the larger of this value and the median residual, so observations further than about 6 * robust_scale_deg from the fit are downweighted. Protects real local rotations (e.g. along faults) from being removed as outliers. Default is 10.

min_data

integer. If the number of observations within distance R_range is less than min_data, a missing value NA will be generated. Default is 3 for circular_idw() and 4 for circular_idw_stats().

min_sq

numeric. Minimum sum of quality x robustness weights of the contributing observations; grid nodes below are dropped.

min_dist_threshold

numeric. Distance threshold for smallest distance of the prediction location to the next observation location. Default is 200 km.

quality_weighting

logical. If a quality weighting should be applied: Default is TRUE. If FALSE, overwrites qp.

qp

numeric. The weighting power of the data quality (the higher the value, the more weight). Default is 1. When set to 0, no weighting is applied.

PoR

Pole of Rotation. data.frame or object of class "euler.pole" containing the geographical coordinates of the Euler pole

PoR_grid

logical. Whether the grid should be generated based on the coordinate range in the PoR (TRUE, the default) CRS or the geographical CRS (FALSE). Is ignored if grid is specified.

remove_PoR

logical. Whether PoR azimuths and coordinates will be removed from final output or not (the default.)

...

Arguments passed to circular_smooth()

Value

sf object with columns

lon, lat

longitude and latitude in degrees

azi

smoothed direction in degrees (0 to 180)

sd

circular standard deviation in degrees

R

search radius in km (for FNN, the effective radius at each node)

mdr

mean distance / R

N

number of contributing observations

sq

sum of quality x robustness weights

Attribute "fit" is a list (one element per R_range) with the observation-level fit: lon, lat, azi_obs, azi_fit, q (quality, scaled so the best observation is 1) and delta (robustness weight; low values mark downweighted outliers).

Details

Based on Hansen & Mount (1990) and Müller, Wehrle, Hettel, Sperner & Fuchs (2003). The predicted direction at a grid node is the weighted circular mean of the fitted observation axes, computed with the same routine as stat = "mean".

Note

Only axial (180° periodic) data are supported.

References

Hansen, K. M., & Mount, V. S. (1990). Smoothing and extrapolation of crustal stress orientation measurements. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth, 95(B2), 1155–1165. https://doi.org/10.1029/JB095iB02p01155

Müller, B., Wehrle, V., Hettel, S., Sperner, B., & Fuchs, K. (2003). A new method for smoothing orientated data and its application to stress data. Geological Society, London, Special Publications, 209(1), 107–126. https://doi.org/10.1144/GSL.SP.2003.209.01.11

See also

compact_grid()

Other smoothing: PoR_idw, idw, krige

Examples

data("san_andreas")
res <- circular_smooth(san_andreas, method = "fsr",
                          R_range = 300, lambda = 0.5)
